memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The thigh that was presented and the breast that was waved must be brought with the fat portions of the food offerings, to be waved before the LORD as a wave offering. This will be the perpetual share for you and your children, as the LORD has commanded.'" - Lev 10:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The perpetual share for you and your children.

On the day two of his children died, Aaron is told about a provision for his children — ongoing, generational, secure.

God speaks about the future when the present has collapsed.

That is characteristic of Him. To Abraham, childless and old, He spoke of descendants like the stars (Gen 15:5). To Israel in exile, with Jerusalem in ruins, He said: I know the plans I have for you... plans to give you hope and a future (Jer 29:11). To Joseph in prison, He gave dreams.

God is never only dealing with today.

This does not erase what has been lost. Nadab and Abihu were still gone. But it says that the story was not over, and that God had not finished with this family.

If you are in a season where the present feels like the end of something, hold on to this. God has always been in the habit of talking about tomorrow while people are still standing in the wreckage of today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I treating a present loss as though it were the end of the story?
2. What has God said about my future that I have stopped believing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when today feels like the end, remind me that You are still speaking about tomorrow. Help me to trust Your long view. Amen.
